feed.subtitle: Posts about Fix, Matchi and the design of testing libraries for Ruby.

entry.title: Fix 1.0 is here
entry.summary: Fix 1.0 is out: a Ruby testing framework where a test suite is an RFC 2119 specification, tested against any subject, each context in its own process.

entry.title: The Three Levels of Requirements Inspired by RFC 2119
entry.summary: How Fix implements the MUST, SHOULD and MAY requirement levels for more precise specifications, and how this compares with RSpec’s historical evolution.

entry.title: Rethinking Test Architecture with Clear Specification Separation
entry.summary: How Fix’s approach to testing in Ruby keeps specifications apart from their implementations, for a test suite that is easier to maintain and to reuse.

entry.title: The Fundamental Distinction Between Expected and Actual Values in Testing
entry.summary: Explore why the distinction between expected and actual values is crucial in test design, and how it impacts the robustness and reliability of your test suite.

entry.title: From RSpec to Fix: A Journey Towards Simpler Testing
entry.summary: How Fix brings simplicity and clarity to Ruby testing with a minimalist approach and an intuitive syntax, compared with traditional frameworks like RSpec.

entry.title: A Fresh Take on Ruby Testing
entry.summary: Introducing Fix 0.7, a minimalist Ruby testing framework focused on clear specifications and pure Ruby objects, built in just 148 lines of code.
